name: Hampi
description: Hampi is the ruined capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, a UNESCO World Heritage Site scattered across a surreal boulder-strewn landscape on the banks of the Tungabhadra River. It suits history enthusiasts, photographers, and budget travellers comfortable with significant walking across uneven terrain; it is not a beach or luxury destination, and the heat from October to May demands early starts.
nearest_airport: Hubli Airport (143 km) or Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru (350 km)

attractions.name: Virupaksha Temple
attractions.description: A living, functioning Shaiva temple that has been in continuous worship since at least the 7th century, anchoring the main Hampi Bazaar strip. The towering 50-metre gopuram is the landmark of Hampi and the interior features a resident elephant, Lakshmi, who blesses visitors.

attractions.name: Vittala Temple & Stone Chariot
attractions.description: The most celebrated monument in Hampi, known for its iconic stone chariot, the musical pillars of the main hall, and the ornate Kalyana Mandapa. It is a 2 km walk or tuk-tuk ride east of Hampi Bazaar along a colonnaded road; entry requires a separate ticket.

attractions.name: Royal Enclosure & Mahanavami Dibba
attractions.description: The walled civic and ceremonial heart of the Vijayanagara capital, containing the Mahanavami Dibba (a three-tiered stone platform for royal ceremonies), the stepped tank, and the Watch Tower. The area is largely open ground with scattered foundations, so context from a guidebook or local guide helps considerably.

attractions.name: Lotus Mahal & Zenana Enclosure
attractions.description: A finely preserved two-storey pavilion in an Indo-Islamic style, tucked inside the walled Zenana Enclosure alongside the Elephant Stables — one of the best-maintained structural complexes in Hampi. Walking distances inside are short and paths are mostly flat, making it suitable for seniors.

attractions.name: Hemakuta Hill Temples
attractions.description: A low hill immediately south of the Virupaksha Temple, dotted with pre-Vijayanagara Jain and Shaiva shrines and offering one of the best unobstructed sunset views over Hampi Bazaar and the Virupaksha gopuram. The climb is gentle and short (about 15 minutes), but the rocky path may be challenging for seniors with mobility issues.

attractions.name: Matanga Hill Sunrise Trek
attractions.description: The highest point in central Hampi, reached by a staircase of several hundred steps, rewarding trekkers with a panoramic 360-degree view of the boulder landscape, Virupaksha Temple, and Tungabhadra River at sunrise. The ascent takes 30–40 minutes and is steep in sections; not suitable for seniors or young children.

attractions.name: Achyutaraya Temple & Sule Bazaar
attractions.description: A large 16th-century temple complex at the foot of Matanga Hill, connected to the river by a long ruined bazaar street — one of the best-preserved ancient market corridors in India. It sees far fewer tourists than Vittala or Virupaksha and the scale and state of abandonment make it quietly powerful.

attractions.name: Tungabhadra River Coracle Ride
attractions.description: A short circular ride in a traditional circular coracle boat across the Tungabhadra, used by locals and tourists to cross between Hampi Bazaar and Virupapur Gadde. The ride itself takes only 10 minutes but offers a distinctive low-on-the-water perspective of the boulder ghats; also the only way to access the north bank village without a long road detour.

attractions.name: Anjaneya Hill (Hanuman's Birthplace)
attractions.description: A moderately steep 575-step climb on the north bank of the Tungabhadra to a small Hanuman temple traditionally identified as the birthplace of Hanuman from the Ramayana. It is a genuine hidden gem — the views rival Matanga Hill but the hill is much less visited, and the path passes through quiet forest with resident langur monkeys.

attractions.name: Sasivekalu Ganesha & Kadalekalu Ganesha
attractions.description: Two colossal open-air monolithic Ganesha sculptures carved from single boulders, located a short walk apart on the slopes below Hemakuta Hill. They are rarely crowded except during festival days and are a good introduction to the scale of Vijayanagara stone carving; walking between them takes only 10 minutes.
